note: Curated list of known open work per bot, regenerated 2026-10-19 from the top entries of KKB-Slim, KKB, Maya, DKB and TRRAIN CHANGELOG.md. The nightly email reads it verbatim; the live test calls and the script checks cannot see these. Remove an item the day it is genuinely closed (a call id proves it).

items.title: Job applications are being refused by the backend
items.what: Since about 6 October the jobs backend refuses applications with HTTP 422 (it rejects the consent field it also requires). The bot asks correctly and calls the apply step; the backend says no. This is not something the bot's script can fix.
items.why: Applying to a job is the point of the call. Callers who say yes are not actually applied.
items.next: Backend team (Sanketika / Signals) to fix the consent field on apply_job. Recorded in KKB-Slim/CHANGELOG.md, 2026-10-12.

items.title: Seven fixes from the 13 October tracker review are live but not yet heard on a call
items.what: Live and checked in the script, but not yet seen on a test call: the education value the backend accepts (r113), the 'already applied' wording (r118), no apply after a failed profile save (r119), a 'yes' to the role check no longer counting as new work (r135), no repeated deep dive after a bare yes (r137), off-topic requests declined in one line (r141), the salary answer (r144), the slower repeat when the caller cannot hear (KI-02), and the 'call me later' output field.
items.why: A change is only proven when a call shows it. Until then these are DEPLOYED, NOT VERIFIED.
items.next: The nightly test calls cover the Slim bots first; a targeted call per fix is still needed for the ones the nightly scenario does not reach.

items.title: Two changes are waiting for a decision, not for a fix
items.what: (1) Tracker r146 asks to move the PIN and landmark questions after the first jobs are read out; that conflicts with KI-12, which needs the PIN first. (2) What to do when a caller under 18 says they are an adult.
items.why: Both change who gets jobs read out and when, so the programme team has to choose.
items.next: Programme team to decide; then route through /update-prompt.

items.title: About half the ITI / polytechnic contacts are blocked as under 18, and the job list has junk rows
items.what: The profile lookup returns U18_NOT_ALLOWED for about half of the ITI and polytechnic campaign contacts. The job list carries duplicates, roles like 'na' or 'Any', Karnataka rows on the Ghaziabad bot, and masked locations.
items.why: Blocked callers cannot be helped at all, and bad rows make the bot read out jobs that are not real options.
items.next: Data team: check the date-of-birth data on the blocked contacts, and clean the job inventory.

items.title: The Hindi Slim bot sometimes wraps its lines in quote marks
items.what: Seen on calls f063e40c and 29771cd5 after the latest Hindi deploys. Not yet traced.
items.why: Usually harmless, but quote marks can change how the voice reads a line.
items.next: Trace which prompt lines teach it (look for quoted spoken lines the model copies).

items.title: Saving the caller's address to their profile only runs while Parth's Mac is on
items.what: The location write-back (scripts/location_writeback.py) runs every 15 minutes from launchd on one Mac. A missed window is caught up only for calls still in the latest 100.
items.why: If the Mac is off for a busy day, some callers' addresses are never saved.
items.next: Move it to a cloud schedule (GitHub Actions now has the Raya secrets) or a server.

items.title: Maya still loses a new caller's consent if they hang up before applying
items.what: Consent is written only when the profile is created at apply time. The KKB Slim fix (save consent at once) was tried on Maya on 13 October and reverted the same day because Maya invented the caller's age 3 times out of 4.
items.why: A caller who agreed but hung up early has no consent on record.
items.next: Re-try with the age asked before the consent question (the order that worked on KKB Slim), then test.

items.title: Maya's education value and age guard are live but not yet heard on a call
items.what: The tester went silent before every apply, so the save step was never reached. MPL removal on the two Signals Maya bots is also DEPLOYED, NOT VERIFIED.
items.why: Unverified until a call reaches the apply step.
items.next: A test call that reaches apply on each Maya Signals bot.

items.title: Maya inbound reads out an old Bengaluru job list
items.what: Inbound Maya offers stale Bengaluru roles (EV roles and similar) to Ghaziabad callers.
items.why: Callers hear jobs they cannot take.
items.next: Point the inbound bot's job source at the current Ghaziabad inventory.

items.title: Two DKB fixes are live but not yet heard on a call
items.what: The truthful line after a failed job post (r130) and 'जी, ज़रूर।' instead of a spoken '(Wait silently)' (r133). r131 is verified on 8cf101ad.
items.why: Unverified until a call shows them.
items.next: Test calls: one with a failed post, one where the owner asks the bot to hold.

items.title: The employer bot cannot save salary or qualification, or close a posting
items.what: The job posting schema has no salary, qualification or experience fields (r115); there is no update or close route (r116); each owner is capped at 5 profiles (r120). A shorter opening pitch (r145, 53% hang up on the current one) needs sign-off for an A/B test.
items.why: Owners give details the system then drops, and cannot close filled jobs.
items.next: Backend team for r115/r116/r120; programme sign-off for the r145 A/B.

items.title: TRRAIN's full 'yes, call me at this time' path has not been heard end to end
items.what: The new offer (ends on a question, only a named time counts as Yes) is verified for silence and refusal. The yes then time then Yes path is VERIFY-PENDING, and the output fix that stores silence as Maybe is DEPLOYED, NOT VERIFIED. Kannada TRRAIN has never run in production.
items.why: The yes path is the one that creates a follow-up for the partner team.
items.next: A test call with a caller who accepts and names a time, on Hindi and on Kannada.

items.title: The older KKB Signals bots carry no live traffic
items.what: Their numbers moved to KKB Slim. Their scripts are kept correct (education values fixed 13 October, DEPLOYED, NOT VERIFIED) so they never regress, and the nightly test calls still dial them.

items.title: What a bot remembers about a caller cannot be read back
items.what: Rules that depend on stored memory (ask the bus stop once, know a job was already applied to) cannot be checked directly, because the platform has no endpoint to read a contact's stored memory.
items.why: Those rules can only be judged indirectly from call behaviour.
items.next: Ask LitWiz for a read-only memory endpoint.

items.title: The test number already has profiles and applications, so it is never a truly new caller
items.what: Every test call reaches the bot from the same test number, which already holds seeker records and applications on most test jobs. 'New caller' scenarios therefore run as returning callers, and apply tests can come back as 'already applied'.
items.why: It can produce false passes and false failures in the nightly calls.
items.next: Have the backend team retire the extra records on the test number, or give the tester a second number.
